grh_b1d274cccce6bb51d842.title: Neither Snow Nor Rain
paragraphs: In a remote mountain community, aging postmaster Cyrus Huddleston learns that Washington intends to close the tiny post office because it handles too little mail. Desperate to preserve both the community gathering place and his daily contact with widow Mildred, whom he secretly loves, Cyrus begins manipulating the mail situation and eventually burns correspondence he does not want delivered. Matters become more tangled when Mildred wins $50,000 through a mailed sweepstakes and starts receiving letters from wealthy Pittsburgh businessman Harris Hughes, who proposes marriage. Jealous Cyrus accuses Hughes of fortune hunting, only to be caught with burning mail and threatened with prosecution. The post office closes despite his efforts, but Cyrus receives a suspended sentence and finally marries Mildred. She admits she never intended to marry Hughes and used the situation to make Cyrus finally declare himself.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on May 28, 1979. It is listed as episode 81 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes John McIntire, Jeanette Nolan, Tom Holland, and Shepard Menken. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, Percy Grainger as writer, and Lorne Greene as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_b1536d05fb74d714cabc.title: The Girl on the Billboard
paragraphs: Television and recording star Lydia Ward returns to her hometown with husband Derek Smith and their young son Wally, only to be confronted by former lover Emory Downs, Wally's biological father, who now wants custody. Wally is kidnapped, Derek is implicated when Emory dies after a fight, and Lydia's pharmacist father is then suspected when poison is found in Emory's medicine. Derek traces the timing of the poison to Emory's home, where Emory's abused wife admits that Emory arranged the kidnapping and planned to flee with the boy and their money; she poisoned him to stop him. Police recover Wally safely in Los Angeles, clearing Lydia's family and ending the visit with the child on his way home.

grh_b17615e20e7267dc39d9.title: Muncy's Mob
paragraphs: Professional golfer Pat Muncie begins an important tournament playing well, but headaches and dizzy spells give way to confusion, angry outbursts and violent behavior that shocks his wife Sharon, his caddy and the gallery known as Muncy's Mob. After Pat assaults people on the course, the case reaches court, where his friend Dr. Theodore Bassett argues that the sudden personality change must have a physical cause. A court-ordered examination reveals a subdural hematoma caused by a seemingly minor bump to Pat's head before the professional rounds began. Surgery succeeds, the assault case is dropped and the PGA welcomes him back. Months later Pat returns to competition and caps his recovery by holing an eagle on the eighteenth hole to win.

grh_b1186666c9c5675acc06.title: Gabriel Starbuck
paragraphs: The people of Yellow Crest quietly decide that aging Sheriff Gabriel Starbuck is no longer capable of protecting the growing town, but Britt cannot bring himself to tell his old friend that they want him replaced. Gabe senses what is happening and secretly takes the bank's money sacks, then rides onto the salt flats and stages the sounds and tracks of a spectacular gun battle with imaginary robbers. Britt witnesses the deception but supports Gabe's story when the townspeople arrive. The town keeps Gabe as sheriff, raises money for a deputy, and Gabe promises Britt that future trouble will be shared with the younger man.

grh_b10d6413cafd515f5842.title: Words at War 43-10-12 (18) Paris - Underground
paragraphs: American widow Etta Shiber and her friend Kitty turn their occupied Paris home into part of an escape network for stranded British soldiers. With forged papers, hospital contacts and help along the demarcation line, they move men toward unoccupied France until betrayal brings arrests. Several members of the network receive prison or death sentences, including Kitty, while Etta is sentenced to hard labor. She is later released in a prisoner exchange for a German spy and closes by honoring Kitty and the resistance work they carried on together.
